chunks: When they entered as their father had advised them, nothing could avail them against (the will of) God, yet it confirmed a premonition Jacob had, for verily he had knowledge as We had taught him, though most men do not know.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Jacob's knowledge in the context of his sons' entry into Egypt?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the distinction between Jacob's divinely granted prophetic knowledge and the limited understanding of the masses, illustrating that external actions (entering Egypt) are subordinate to internal divine decree. The phrase 'a need in his soul' is interpreted by scholars as the fulfillment of the promise that his son Joseph would survive, demonstrating how God's will operates through both visible events and hidden spiritual realities. This highlights the concept of 'Ilm al-Ghayb' (knowledge of the unseen) granted to the Prophets, contrasting it with the general human condition.
